adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs + routes/group-members.js.es6 — the public group members page lost all pagination affordances and is now hard-capped at the model's default limit (50), a functional regression vs. the previous unpaginated (for non-automatic groups) listing — groups with >50 members can no longer show the rest. (confidence 85, P1)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the endpoint now **always** applies `limit`/`offset` (default `limit = 50`, `offset = 0`) for all groups: `members = group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. Previously, pagination (limit/offset) was only applied for `automatic?` groups; non-automatic groups returned the full list. On the client, `routes/group-members.js.es6` now sets the controller model to the group and calls `model.findMembers()`, and the template `group/members.hbs` iterates `{{#each m in members}}`. However, no pagination controls/actions were added for the public group members page to change `offset` and re-fetch. As a result, groups with >50 members will only ever show the first 50 with no affordance to view the rest—this is a functional regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:19-35 — `members` action's response shape changed from a flat array to `{members:, meta:{total,limit,offset}}` with unconditional pagination, but spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb does not exist anywhere in the repo — zero test coverage for this behavioral change. (confidence 90, P1)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a real behavioral change in `GroupsController#members`: it now returns a JSON object with `{ members, meta }` and applies limit/offset for all groups, whereas previously it rendered a flat serialized array (with pagination only for automatic groups). However, the proposed finding’s main claim—“spec/controllers/groups_controller_spec.rb does not exist anywhere in the repo” and therefore “zero test coverage”—is not verifiable from this diff. The diff only shows changes to `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`, and does not prove absence of a non-admin groups controller spec elsewhere. Also, lack of tests is not itself a defect introduced by the diff unless the absence is demonstrably new/broken, which is not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:20-21 — `limit`/`offset` are read via bare `.to_i` with no upper/lower clamp before being passed to `.limit().offset()`. (confidence 55, P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff changes pagination to always apply `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, and then directly calls `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)`. There is no clamp on `limit` (e.g., max page size) and no validation of `offset` being non-negative. This means a client can request an arbitrarily large `limit` and potentially cause heavy DB load / large responses (and negative offsets may behave unexpectedly depending on AR/version). This is a real issue introduced/present in the diff (lack of input bounding before limit/offset).

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:71 — `usernames.split(",").each` doesn't `.strip` or de-duplicate entries; unmatched/blank usernames are silently skipped with no feedback to the admin. (confidence 55, P3)

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code takes `usernames = params.require(:usernames)` and iterates `usernames.split(",").each do |username|` without trimming whitespace or filtering blanks/duplicates. This is verifiable in the diff: if the client sends "alice, bob" (note space) or trailing commas, `User.find_by_username(username)` will not match for entries like " bob" or "", and those entries will be silently ignored. The action still returns `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, so the admin gets no indication that some provided usernames were not added.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `addMembers`/`removeMember` returning `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` without any local rejection handling, and the admin controller actions don’t attach a `.catch`. However, the finding’s claim that failures “fail completely silently with no UI feedback” is not verifiable from this diff alone: `Discourse.ajax` commonly provides centralized error handling in Discourse, and nothing in the diff demonstrates that errors would be swallowed. Also, the UI hides add/remove member controls for `automatic` groups (`{{#unless automatic}}...{{/unless}}`), so the cited 422 automatic-group scenario would not normally be triggered via the new UI. This reads more like a general robustness suggestion than a clear defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication.rationale: In `group.hbs` the member rows are rendered via `{{each member in members itemView="group-member"}}`, and the per-row template `group_member.hbs` uses `{{#unless automatic}}` to decide whether to show the remove link. The new `group-member` view (`views/group-member.js.es6`) does not define/pass through an `automatic` property from the parent controller/group model, so in the itemView template `automatic` will be looked up on the row context (the member/User or the view) where it is not defined. In Ember/Handlebars, an undefined property is falsy, so `{{#unless automatic}}` will evaluate as true and the remove button can render even for automatic groups (guard becomes ineffective).
